text: When Sanballat and Tobiah, along with the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the men of Ashdod, heard that the repair of the walls of Jerusalem was moving ahead and that the gaps were being closed, they were furious.
They all conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
But we prayed to our God, and because of the threat we posted a guard against them day and night.

versions.text: But we prayed to our God, and because of them we posted a guard against them day and night.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a doubled reference ("against them... from before them"), but rendering both as "them" in English produces an awkward, redundant line for oral reading. Naming the threat once keeps the sense while smoothing the rhythm.

text: Meanwhile the people of Judah said, "The strength of the laborers is failing, and there is far too much rubble; we cannot rebuild the wall."
And our enemies said, "Before they know it or see a thing, we will be in among them. We will kill them and put an end to the work."
Then the Jews who lived near them came and warned us ten times over, "Wherever you turn, they will come against us."
So I stationed men in the lowest places behind the wall, at the exposed points, positioning them by families with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

I looked things over, then rose and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: "Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew of their scheme and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to his own work.
From that day on, half of my men did the work while the other half stood ready with spears, shields, bows, and armor; and the officers took their place behind all the people of Judah

versions.text: From that day on, half of my men worked on the building while the other half stood ready with spears, shields, bows, and armor; and the officers took their place behind all the people of Judah
versions.explanation: בַּמְּלָאכָה is "the work" in general (matching "the work" language throughout the chapter), not specifically "the building"; the change also avoids ambiguity with the builders mentioned in the next verse.

text: who were building the wall. Those who carried loads worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other,
and each of the builders worked with his sword strapped to his waist. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.

versions.text: and each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he worked. The man who sounded the trumpet stayed at my side.
versions.explanation: The repetition of "at his side... at my side" in consecutive clauses is distracting when read aloud; "waist" also renders מָתְנָיו more precisely.

text: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, "The work is vast and spread out, and we are far apart from one another along the wall.
Wherever you hear the trumpet sound, rally to us there. Our God will fight for us!"
So we carried on the work, half of the men holding spears, from the first light of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also told the people, "Let every man and his servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may stand guard for us by night and work by day."
Neither I nor my brothers nor my men nor the guards with me ever took off our clothes; each of us kept his weapon at hand, even when going for water.
